items.title: Define and implement stable task-plus-agent identity resolution
items.context: Follow Workstream D and the shipped owner-session contract. Resolution remains explicit override, validated host-adapter task+agent identity, bounded generated fallback, then warned derived-ppid fallback. Do not use a repository-global token or collapse reviewer and implementer privileges.
items.userSees: User sees "owner session: <stable-id> [host-adapter]" remain unchanged across same-task shell boundaries; a different task or role sees the existing foreign-owner rejection.

adversarial.desc: Precedence and validation attack: with a deliberate non-empty LATTICE_SESSION_ID plus conflicting host-native task/agent values, resolution must use the explicit override; without the override, an adapter candidate is accepted only when both taskIdentity and agentOrRoleIdentity are validated. Missing, empty, malformed, provider-mismatched, or one-dimensional host input must not be promoted to host-adapter identity and must fall through in order without a host-specific core exception.

Collision and privilege attack: for identical project/worktree, provider, taskIdentity, and agentOrRoleIdentity, changing PPID/process ancestry must leave the resolved host-adapter identity unchanged; changing only taskIdentity or only agentOrRoleIdentity must produce a different identity. A repository-global token, worktree-only token, thread-only token, or role-collapsed identity fails; implementer, verification-intent, reviewer, and delivery identities must not inherit each others owner privilege unless canonical policy explicitly allows shared ownership.

Fallback-boundary attack: when validated adapter identity is unavailable, generated fallback must be opaque and bounded by project, provider, task, agent/role, and adapter session boundary so separate tasks, roles, or sessions cannot collide; derived-ppid may occur only after explicit, validated-adapter, and generated paths are unavailable, must remain PPID-sensitive, and must be reported as degraded with a warning before the first story-scoped mutation.

Disclosure and enforcement attack: raw host task/session/agent tokens and generated token material must not appear in the derived session id, session_brief/doctor output, owner errors, process events, story metadata, requirements prose, or other material artifacts; diagnostics may expose only stable opaque/redacted identity plus source/provider metadata. A genuinely different task-or-role identity attempting an owner-gated mutation must still fail closed with established active/stale takeover guidance, while read-only and reviewerWrite boundaries remain unchanged.

items.title: Propagate stable identity through supported host adapters and diagnostics
items.context: Codex, Claude, and agy adapter paths must retain task and agent/role identity across child shells without exposing raw host tokens. session_brief and mutation warnings must report the identity source and degraded derived-ppid fallback.
items.userSees: User sees "session identity degraded: derived-ppid" with an actionable LATTICE_SESSION_ID/adapter hint before the first owner-gated mutation; supported adapters report their provider and source without raw tokens.

items.title: Prove isolation, compatibility, and takeover behavior with bounded regressions
items.context: Cover same task/agent across PPID changes, different tasks in one repository, implementer versus reviewer separation, explicit override, genuine foreign lease blocking, stale/active takeover, degraded warning, and supported adapter cases without live-host dependence where deterministic seams suffice.
items.userSees: User sees the same established stale/active takeover guidance for a genuine foreign lease, while same-task shell changes proceed without "foreign owner".

adversarial.desc: With deterministic resolver inputs holding project/worktree, taskIdentity, agentOrRoleIdentity, and adapter session boundary constant while shell and ppid values change, every invocation resolves the same opaque owner id and refreshes the existing lease without a foreign-owner rejection; the test must fail if ppid leaks into a validated task-plus-agent identity.

With the same repository, worktree, provider, and agent identity but two independent task identities, deterministic adapter/generated-token seams resolve different owner ids; each task can own its own story, and neither task can inherit or refresh the other task owner lease through a repository-global or thread-only token.

Within one task/thread, implementer, verification-intent, reviewer, and delivery agent/role inputs resolve distinct identities unless an explicit canonical shared-ownership policy fixture says otherwise; reviewer or intent identity cannot refresh, seize, or count as the implementer owner merely because provider, task, thread, worktree, or parent process matches.

A trimmed non-empty explicit LATTICE_SESSION_ID deterministically wins conflicting adapter, generated-token, and ppid inputs across parent changes, while a blank/whitespace override is ignored; diagnostics identify explicit-env without exposing raw native host tokens or promoting the override to authentication/reviewer/Authority proof.

For an active lease owned by a genuinely different resolved task-plus-agent session, every ordinary story-scoped mutation fails closed and preserves the established error facts: story, owner id/cwd/heartbeat, ACTIVE verdict, current session, and read-only/wait/--forceTakeover guidance; same-worktree proximity must not bypass the block.

Identity stabilization does not change takeover semantics: a stale foreign lease transfers only with explicit --takeover and an auditable event; an active foreign lease rejects ordinary mutation and --takeover, transferring only through deliberate --forceTakeover or the canonical human-approved path, with ownership and heartbeat updated atomically.

When explicit env, validated adapter identity, and generated-token seams are all absent, deterministic hostname/root/ppid inputs use derived-ppid only: changing ppid changes the id, session_brief/doctor label the source degraded, and an actionable export-LATTICE_SESSION_ID/use-supported-adapter warning appears before the first owner-gated mutation rather than falsely treating shell changes as one session.

Table-driven deterministic seams for Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, Antigravity, and agy prove that each adapter maps stable task plus agent/role inputs to the canonical resolver across ppid changes, separates changed task/role/session-boundary inputs, preserves provider as diagnostics only, redacts raw host tokens, and requires no live-host call or provider-specific branch in generic lease logic.

For a supported adapter without a native stable signal, generated-token fixtures reuse one opaque id only within the same project, provider, task, agent/role, and adapter session boundary; changing any isolation dimension does not collide, persisted state follows registered runtime-artifact cleanup/material-hygiene rules, and raw tokens never enter story evidence or logs.

Legacy readable lease source labels are normalized through the canonical resolver without changing the stored owner identity, granting role/task privilege, or bypassing foreign-owner checks; active/stale classification and takeover guidance remain identical for a legacy lease fixture and its canonical equivalent.

items.title: Ratify the canonical task-and-agent identity contract before runtime implementation
items.context: Before any runtime code change, record understanding and a structured decision with at least three adversarial pre-mortem scenarios, explicitly update or confirm the canonical owner-session identity contract, and obtain fresh review evidence from at least two independent real hosts as required by Workstream D. This decision must settle task identity, role separation, resolution priority, fallback storage/cleanup, observability, and non-goals.
items.userSees: User sees "two-host owner-session contract review: PASS (codex + antigravity; local assurance only)" before runtime implementation begins.
excludes: No runtime owner-session implementation begins before the decision and independent-host review evidence are accepted.

happy.desc: Read decision_get for B-62b8 and the current canonical owner-session document: the structured decision selects taskIdentity + agentOrRoleIdentity, contains at least three concrete trigger/consequence/mitigation pre-mortems, and the document explicitly settles canonical LATTICE_SESSION_ID consumption, role separation, resolution priority (explicit override -> validated host-adapter composite -> bounded generated token -> warned derived-ppid), generated-token scope/storage/ownership/cleanup, runtime-artifact/material-hash exclusion, source/provider observability without raw tokens, unchanged stale/active takeover semantics, and non-goals forbidding authentication, Authority/reviewer/production proof, repository-global tokens, and provider branches in generic core. WHY: implementation may begin only from a complete, ratified contract rather than an implicit runtime choice.

A fresh independent real Codex CLI review of the final current owner-session document returns PASS on every contract dimension and records hostProvider=codex, a non-empty reviewer/session id, storyId=B-62b8, command or transcript identifier/hash, timestamp, exact current git HEAD, exact current material hash, and exact SHA-256 of the reviewed document; it explicitly labels the result localAssuranceOnly=true and disclaims Authority, authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, release, and production-completion claims. WHY: Workstream D requires independent real-host ratification bound to exactly the artifact implemented.

A fresh independent real Antigravity/agy CLI review of the same final current owner-session document returns PASS on every contract dimension and records hostProvider=antigravity or agy, a non-empty reviewer/session id distinct from the Codex reviewer/session, storyId=B-62b8, command or transcript identifier/hash, timestamp, the same exact current git HEAD, material hash, and document SHA-256 as the Codex review; it explicitly labels the result localAssuranceOnly=true and disclaims Authority, authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, release, and production-completion claims. WHY: two different real host providers and sessions are required; two invocations of one host do not establish host independence.

edge.desc: Review the boundary cases in the decision and document: blank/unvalidated adapter inputs do not collapse tasks or roles, generated tokens are bounded by project+provider+task+agent-or-role and have explicit ownership/cleanup/doctor/session_brief behavior, derived-ppid remains last-resort and visibly warned before mutation, and legacy foreign/stale/active lease takeover rules remain unchanged and audited. WHY: apparent shell stability must not create a repository-wide privilege or alter established recovery behavior.

Recompute git HEAD, the repository material hash via the canonical Lattice mechanism, and SHA-256 of docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md after the final document commit; accept both host PASS records only when all three bindings exactly match those recomputed values and both timestamps/reviews postdate that final version. WHY: a PASS over an earlier document or material state cannot authorize implementation of the current contract.

adversarial.desc: Attempt to qualify evidence with any stale or mismatched HEAD/material/document hash, missing binding, FAIL/non-PASS verdict, synthetic/non-real host, same provider twice, same reviewer/session twice, or review of a different story/document; the acceptance result excludes it and CHK-004 remains unratified. WHY: loosely related transcripts must never satisfy the two-host prerequisite.

Inspect both transcripts and all resulting summaries for claims that local host review proves authentication, reviewer attestation, Authority evidence, authorityDone/fullAuthorityDone, release readiness, or production completion; any such claim fails acceptance even when both reviewers say PASS. WHY: two-host local review is explicitly local assurance only.

Before the structured decision, final document binding, and both qualifying independent-host PASS records are accepted, git diff/history for this story shows no runtime/code/test implementation attributed to CHK-001 through CHK-003; if prerequisites are absent or invalid, implementation remains blocked rather than waived. WHY: Workstream D requires contract ratification before runtime implementation begins.
